newsitem.title: USA: Labor Dept economist - US jobs gains widespread - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Labor Dept economist - US jobs gains widespread - RFTV.

text.p: Labor Department economist Joseph Meisenheimer said job gains reflected in the December employment report ran across a wide range of industries.

"The increases were really widespread," Meisenheimer said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "Virtually every major industry -- except for mining which typically loses jobs just about every month -- every other major industry showed at least some growth however small."
"Overall I think it was really a strong report," Meisenheimer.
The 262,000 jobs created last month exceeded the expectations of Wall Street analysts who were looking for about 192,000 new jobs.

Average hourly earnings by workers, closely watched because of the role wage-inflation plays in pushing up consumer prices, rose six cents an hour last month after rising nine cents an hour in November.
Meisenheimer said two large back-to-back increases in hourly earnings might "cause concern among some people." Wage growth in 1996 was "quite a bit stronger" than in 1995 and 1994, he said.

Meisenheimer said warm weather might have contributed to more hiring than normal for early winter. The retail sector had hired holiday help early in the season, reflecting a decline in December after seasonal adjustment, he said.
"After the seasonal adjustment process takes place it made it appear as if there was actually a decline in merchandise stores," he said.
